title: Account-weighted roadmap queue and SLA-triggered escalation logic
creator: Nadia Chen
description:
Problem: Top-account feature asks and escalations are currently tracked in disparate spreadsheets and Slack threads, leading to ad-hoc prioritization and ad-hoc hotfixes that bypass roadmap discipline. We need a repeatable, auditable intake + prioritization process that (1) weights requests by account strategic value and usage signals, (2) ties escalation eligibility to SLA breach or operational impact, and (3) surfaces prioritized items into the product roadmap with transparent rationale for engineering/resource allocation.

Goal: Build an "account-weighted roadmap queue" that computes a per-request priority score and an "SLA-triggered escalation logic" module that promotes items to an expedited pipeline when predefined service thresholds are violated. Deliverables: scoring formula and config, intake form template, routing rules, escalation thresholds and remediation playbook, and a small dashboard for PM/AE visibility.

Scope decisions and trade-offs:
- Scoring will combine ARR-weighted account score (40%), active usage delta (20%), number/frequency of production incidents (20%), executive sponsorship/strategic-fit (10%), and product-fit complexity (10%). We considered a purely votes-based system but rejected it because it underweights enterprise ARR and incident severity.
- Escalation will be SLA-binary: incidents that meet SLA breach criteria or cause critical degradation move immediately to "Expedite" with automatic assignment to an on-call SRE + product lead. Less-severe issues can be fast-tracked via PM review.
- We will not at first attempt machine-learning ranking; initial implementation uses deterministic scoring so it's auditable and easy to explain to customers.

Data sources: ARR and renewal dates from SFDC export, usage signals from telemetry (Prod metrics dashboard), incident count from PagerDuty, customer relationship notes from CSMs (Drive doc), and existing roadmap commitments in roadmap-2026.Q2.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
1) Intake form (Drive) + GitHub-backed intake ticket template created and in use by at least 3 CSM/AE teams.
2) Scoring engine implemented as a serverless function that tags intake tickets with a priority level (P0-P3) and produces an explainable breakdown.
3) Escalation logic integrated with PagerDuty/SLO alerts so that qualifying incidents automatically create an expedited ticket and notify a rotation of PM+SRE.
4) Dashboard in Console (internal) that lists top-100 prioritized customer asks and shows score components and status.

Key links and artifacts:
- PRD (draft): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1A2b_AccountWeightedPRD 
- Intake template (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/account-roadmap-intake 
- Prototype scoring spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ScoringPrototype 
- GitHub sample implementation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/roadmap-intake/tree/pm-5530 
- PagerDuty playbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/PD+Escalation+Playbook

Rollout plan: Beta with 5 strategic accounts for 4 weeks (Apr 1-Apr 30) to validate score calibration and escalation noise. After beta, iterate and expand to all enterprise accounts by mid-Q2.

next_steps: Finish GH PR and deploy scoring lambda to staging. Coordinate SFDC read access with Revenue Ops. Run calibration with beta account data and collect feedback from CSMs. Draft post-beta acceptance criteria and budget for Q2 implementation. Schedule cross-functional review 2026-03-18.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: over-escalation causing alert fatigue and wasted engineering cycles. Mitigation: require incident frequency and impact threshold before automatic expedite; initial rollout limited to 5 accounts; include an override/appeal workflow for AEs/CSMs. Monitor false-positive rate and tune scoring weights.
notes_for_reviewers: When reviewing scoring weights, focus on ARR vs incident sensitivity trade-off. We aim to prefer a conservative escalation policy at launch; calibration will be driven by beta metrics (false positive rate, mean time to resolution improvement, customer satisfaction delta).
